proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1204, when must an exit door swing outward in the direction of exit travel?

options.text: Whenever the room serves more than 10 occupants regardless of occupancy type or storey
Whenever the occupant load served by the door is 50 or more persons
Only when the door opens directly onto a public street or exterior sidewalk
Only for assembly and institutional occupancies; offices and storage are exempted

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1204 requires exit doors to swing outward (in the direction of exit travel) when serving an occupant load of 50 or more persons. Below 50 persons inward swinging is permitted. The 50-person threshold applies universally — it is not limited to assembly or institutional uses.
proposed.explanation: The outward-swing rule at 50 persons prevents crowd crush against a door that would swing into a crowd. The threshold is 50 — not 10, not 100. Any answer suggesting occupancy-type restrictions is incorrect.
